tasks.name: mangle-8edad8d3-blind30
tasks.environment_mermaid:
flowchart LR
  A["Base image golang 1.25 pinned by digest"] --> B["google mangle checkout at a pinned commit"]
  A --> C["tmux and python3 installed"]
  D["30 single-line faults copied over 23 source files"] --> B
  B --> E["Test files deleted and build cache rewarmed on the faulted tree"]
  F["Instruction.md with a behavioural symptom report"] --> G["Agent session as agent user, no network"]
  E --> G
  C --> G
  G --> H["Repaired tree plus rca.json and RESEARCH_AND_PLANNING.md"]
  H --> I["Shared verifier runs as root in the same container"]
  I --> J["Hidden Go suite restored and run with go test"]
  I --> K["rca.json compared with the 30-entry answer key"]
  J --> L["Repair and report halves weighted 0.5 each"]
  K --> L
  L --> M["Reward written to /logs/verifier"]
environment_facts: The image builds from a digest-pinned golang base, clones google/mangle at commit 8edad8d3, downloads all modules and adds tmux and python3; the run has no network, 2 CPUs and 8 GB of memory (environment/Dockerfile, task.toml).

Thirty injected faults are copied over 23 files in packages such as analysis, engine, provenance, symbols and factstore, and the repository's test files are deleted so the agent has no suite to run (environment/Dockerfile, task.toml).
The Go build cache warmed on the pristine checkout is emptied and rewarmed on the faulted tree, so cached objects cannot reveal the original code (environment/Dockerfile).

The verifier runs as root in the agent's own container, restores the hidden suite from the root-owned tests mount and runs go test -count=1 ./... as the agent account, against a baseline of 382 passing tests (task.toml, tests/grade.py, tests/answer_key.json).

The reward is half repair (the suite passes and nothing else broke) and half report (rca.json names each edited file and function), with canary and determinism checks against forged results (tests/grade.py, tests/answer_key.json).
The agent must write /app/RESEARCH_AND_PLANNING.md before editing code, and the worktree, rca.json and plan are collected as artifacts (instruction.md, task.toml).
tasks.workflow: A maintainer of a Datalog engine receives a user report that undocumented single-line edits have broken parsing, type checking, evaluation, provenance and temporal arithmetic, and no test suite is available. The maintainer starts from the faulted source tree and the written symptoms only. The hard part is tracing each symptom to the function that holds the edit, including symptoms that need two separate fixes before they disappear, and then naming exactly those functions in a root-cause report.
tasks.prompt_pattern: A first-person symptom report grouped by subsystem and written in user terms without function names, followed by a request to restore the behavior, a JSON schema for `/app/rca.json` with one file and function per edit, and a requirement to write `/app/RESEARCH_AND_PLANNING.md` before touching code.

tasks.name: torchio-canonical
tasks.environment_mermaid:
flowchart LR
  A["Base image python 3.12 pinned by digest"] --> B["venv with torch CPU, SimpleITK, NiBabel, zarr and pytest"]
  A --> C["tmux, git and asciinema"]
  D["TorchIO 2.0.0a2 tree with injected implementation drift"] --> E["Sanitized one-commit repository in /workdir"]
  B --> F["Agent session as agent, no network"]
  C --> F
  E --> F
  G["Instruction.md naming in-scope code and docs"] --> F
  F --> H["Final /workdir copied out as artifact"]
  H --> I["Separate verifier image with the same toolchain"]
  I --> J["Documentation preservation check"]
  I --> K["Sealed cases run as nobody in fresh interpreters"]
  J --> L["40 fault groups and 36 regression groups scored"]
  K --> L
  L --> M["Binary and partial reward written to /logs/verifier"]
environment_facts: The agent image uses a digest-pinned Python base with /opt/venv holding exact versions of PyTorch for CPU, NumPy, SimpleITK, NiBabel, nifti-zarr, zarr, matplotlib and pytest; torchio itself is imported from /workdir/src through PYTHONPATH (environment/Dockerfile).

/workdir holds TorchIO at commit 2b019d2a with documentation curation and selected drift already applied, committed as a single sanitized commit with no remotes, tags or reflog (environment/Dockerfile).

The agent has 4 hours with no network; the verifier is a separate container built from tests/Dockerfile that repeats the agent toolchain and receives only the final /workdir (task.toml, tests/Dockerfile).

Before running any candidate code, the grader checks that in-scope documentation pages, docstrings and comments are unchanged against a sealed digest, then runs private cases as the nobody user with the candidate src appended after site-packages (tests/grade.py, tests/doc_digest.py, tests/private/driver.py).

Observations are compared with sealed expected values in 40 fail-to-pass and 36 pass-to-pass groups; the partial reward is the mean F2P fraction times the mean P2P fraction, and the binary reward is 1 only when every group passes (tests/grade.py, tests/private_manifest.json, tests/reward_writer.py).
tasks.workflow: A maintainer of a medical imaging library treats the documentation as the specification and repairs the places where the code has drifted from it. The engineer starts from the source tree with its pages, docstrings and examples, and has no list of the discrepancies. The hard part is reading a large documented surface of transforms, data containers and patch sampling closely enough to find each behavioral mismatch, fixing the code rather than the docs, and leaving every behavior that already matches untouched.
tasks.prompt_pattern: A short description of the library, a one-line directive to fix implementation drift from the documentation, an explicit list of in-scope source paths and documentation pages, a rule that documentation outranks code and comments, and a note on the installed offline environment.

tasks.name: terraform-centralwatch-alert-routing-module-refactor
tasks.environment_mermaid:
flowchart LR
  A["Base image debian bookworm slim"] --> B["Pinned terraform 1.16.4, provider mirror and conftest"]
  B --> C["Flat count-indexed stack in /workspace/infra"]
  C --> D["Production state copy and CI guardrail policies"]
  E["Instruction.md with layout, keys, variables and outputs"] --> F["Agent session as agent, no network or AWS access"]
  D --> F
  F --> G["Refactored infra directory collected as artifact"]
  G --> H["Separate verifier with terraform, conftest and hcl2json"]
  H --> I["Offline init, validate and plan against pristine state"]
  I --> J["Gates for moves-only plan, policies, static bans and pasted IDs"]
  J --> K["Second plan on a state with swapped IDs"]
  K --> L["46 requirement checks from spec.json"]
  L --> M["Partial reward written to /logs/verifier"]
environment_facts: Agent and verifier images share a debian bookworm-slim base with terraform 1.16.4, the AWS 5.100.0 and archive 2.8.1 providers in an offline filesystem mirror, and conftest 0.70.1, each checksum-verified (environment/Dockerfile, tests/Dockerfile).

The starting repository is a flat root module of about 260 AWS resources across 9 services with a production terraform.tfstate copy, a plan_safety.rego policy and scripts/ci-plan.sh, committed once and planned clean at build time (environment/Dockerfile, environment/infra/README.md, task.toml).
Provider traffic is routed to a dead loopback proxy and the task has no network, so no AWS call can succeed (environment/Dockerfile, task.toml).
The verifier discards state, plan and lock files from the artifact and plans offline as nobody against its own pristine state (tests/grade.py, tests/test.sh).

Any failed gate gives 0: offline init, validate and plan, static bans, a moves-only plan, CI policies, no pasted IDs, a remapped-state plan and outputs as plain module references; otherwise the reward is the fraction of 46 checks passed (tests/grade.py, task.toml).
tasks.workflow: A platform engineer inherits a production alert-routing stack written as one flat root module with list-indexed resources and hard-coded settings. The engineer must split it into eventing, messaging and processing modules keyed by team, source, severity and channel, with generalized variables and outputs. The hard part is expressing every address change in configuration so the plan against the live state contains only moves, while passing IDs between modules through outputs instead of literals.
tasks.prompt_pattern: A first-person request to modularize a named Terraform stack without changing running infrastructure, followed by long constraint sections on how CI judges the change, module layout and ownership, `for_each` keys, root variables, root outputs and banned constructs.

tasks.name: pdk-actual-sync-log-checkpoint-compaction
tasks.environment_mermaid:
flowchart LR
  A["Base image node 22 bookworm"] --> B["Actual monorepo at a pinned commit"]
  A --> C["Yarn 4 through corepack, sqlite3 and tmux"]
  B --> D["Dependencies installed and four packages built"]
  E["Instruction.md with the checkpoint protocol"] --> F["Agent session as agent, no internet"]
  C --> F
  D --> F
  F --> G["git diff against base saved as model.patch"]
  G --> H["Separate verifier container applies the patch"]
  H --> I["Hidden test patch staged in a root-only directory"]
  I --> J["Hidden node suite run as sdapp"]
  J --> K["8 fail-to-pass tests and 2 gated guards"]
  K --> L["Reward written to /logs/verifier"]
environment_facts: The agent image is node:22-bookworm pinned by digest with Yarn 4.17.1 through corepack, sqlite3, tmux and asciinema; actualbudget/actual is fetched at commit 832f43da, installed with yarn install --immutable and built for the crdt, core, sync-server and api workspaces (environment/Dockerfile).

The solver runs as an unprivileged agent user for up to 12 hours with no internet, 4 CPUs and 8 GB of memory, and may start installed services only through a restricted sudo wrapper (task.toml, environment/Dockerfile).
After the run, staged changes are diffed against the base commit with external diff and textconv disabled and saved as /logs/artifacts/model.patch (task.toml).

A separate verifier image rebuilds the same repository, adds protobuf client libraries for the grader, applies the submission and a hidden test patch, and runs the hidden suite as the unprivileged sdapp user (tests/Dockerfile, tests/test.sh, tests/grader-node/package.json).
The reward is 1 only when all 8 fail-to-pass tests pass and the 2 gated pass-to-pass guards still pass; a partial F2P fraction is also written (tests/config.json, tests/grader.py).
tasks.workflow: A backend engineer on a self-hosted budgeting app needs the sync server to compact each budget's change log from a client-built snapshot without breaking offline devices. The engineer starts from the sync server, CRDT and client packages, and the server cannot read the encrypted changes it stores. The hard part is the protocol: a conditional checkpoint commit tied to a receive base, correct handling of late messages with older timestamps, and compatibility for old clients, all checked across several simulated devices.
tasks.prompt_pattern: A product-style problem statement followed by `What we need`, `Keep working` and `Setup` sections that fix the environment variable, protobuf field numbers, HTTP headers, endpoint and status codes, and the build commands.

tasks.prompt_pattern: A paragraph stating the current insecure behavior, a bullet list of observable requirements with time limits and HTTP status codes, and a closing paragraph on services, the offline build command and what is out of scope.
